question.text: Mr. Harish Varadarajan runs 'Kaveri SME Fund' (Cat I SME AIF). He is debating a thesis note with the IC on whether to use a long-short listed-equity overlay to hedge the SME book. Per Chapter 9 and the Cat I/II framework, what is the correct position?

answer.text: Yes, the fund can deploy 2x leverage and long-short overlays identical to Cat III.

No — long-short / market-neutral / global-macro strategies are Cat III strategies. A Cat I/II SME Fund must stick to Cat I/II-native strategies (PE equity, VC, mezzanine, growth) and cannot replicate Cat III hedge overlays.
Yes, provided the overlay is under 5% of NAV.

explanation.text: The Logic: Category III AIFs are defined by employment of complex/diverse trading strategies including leverage and long-short/arbitrage. Category I and II funds do not use leverage and do not employ such complex trading operations as part of their core investment mandate. SME Funds qualify under Category I, so an SME Fund is expected to follow Cat I/II-native strategies (PE equity, VC, mezzanine, growth), not Cat III hedge-style overlays. The Trap: Options A and C invent leverage allowances or size-based carve-outs that do not exist for Category I/II funds under the framework. Option D is a nonsense distractor. Note: Always test a proposed strategy against the Category I/II versus Category III strategy distinction in the workbook before approving it for a Cat I SME Fund.
